{"completeness": 0.65, "citation_quality": 0.4, "severity_defensibility": 0.75, "overall_pass": false, "feedback": "The investigation has significant gaps that prevent passing review. The ATT&CK technique citation is poorly justified—T1189 (Drive-by Compromise) refers to malicious websites that compromise visitors, not XSS injection attempts against web applications, which better align with T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) or T1598 (Phishing). The severity assessment, while defensible given successful quarantine, undersells the critical alert designation without explaining why the SOC initially marked it critical or whether that escalation was warranted. The investigation lacks completeness on several fronts: no analysis of whether the malicious payload had any sophisticated obfuscation or encoded content, no investigation into whether the same IP or Tor exit node has targeted this application before, and no evidence collection details (e.g., how the Tor exit node was identified, whether geo-intelligence corroborates threat actor profiles). The recommendation to 'monitor for repeat attempts' is generic and doesn't specify thresholds or trigger points for escalation. Strengthen the response by selecting correct ATT&CK techniques with explicit reasoning, reconciling the alert severity with the actual risk posture, and providing more specific post-incident monitoring parameters."}
